title: Checkpoint classification treats missing evidence and isolated passes as solved
reasoning: passed_chkpt is true when either pass rate reaches one or the counts match. Missing counts default to zero, so even a row with strict_pass_rate=0 and no counts is classified as passed. An isolated_pass_rate of one also overrides an explicit strict failure. These flags feed filtered passed-checkpoint and solved-problem calculations, overstating success under the required strict all-cases criterion. The existing test establishes that strict success is sufficient, but does not establish that isolated success or missing evidence may override strict failure.
reproduction: Call process_checkpoint_row with {'strict_pass_rate': 0.0}, or with strict_pass_rate=0.5, isolated_pass_rate=1.0, total_tests=10, passed_tests=5. Both return passed_chkpt=True.
recommendation: Make verified strict all-cases success authoritative and classify missing or incomplete pass evidence as unsolved; do not allow isolated results to override strict failure.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The only direct classification test checks strict_pass_rate=1.0. It does not cover strict failures, conflicting evidence, missing counts, or zero evaluated tests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand checkpoint-classification coverage into a matrix of strict success, strict failure, isolated-only success, missing evidence, and zero-test rows, preserving the existing strict-success scenario.
minimumFixScope: process_checkpoint_row and its existing behavioral test coverage.
